title: “Stop the Count!”—How Reporting Partial Election Results Fuels Beliefs in Election Fraud
evidence_summary: The human report identifies two Study 5 partial-eta-squared reporting discrepancies: lead .01 versus code .004, and candidate <.01 versus code .012; F statistics and p-values recur.
notes: P2 numerical reporting differences, not a failed substantive conclusion. The final 2025 published article p.684 retains .01 and <.01, verified against the publisher PDF. The report calls the study Vaz et al. (2024); use the verified 2025 DOI/year. Public Rmd, rendered HTML and seven CSV inputs inventoried. Screening eligibility only: independently adjudicate 5–8 claims, tolerances and laptop runtime before the draw. No complete statistical workflow rerun in round 2.

title: Battling the coronavirus ‘infodemic’ among social media users in Kenya and Nigeria

notes: Only the shipped R analysis stage with cached author-provided probabilities is eligible. Regenerating those probabilities took >5 h and is excluded from the benchmark run. The source repaired table-formatting gsub calls only; do not use its accelerated/reworked Python simulation as original-code evidence. Original Rmd has set.seed(60637), but selects between two shipped cleaned-data RDS files by filesystem mtime. Pin the intended input explicitly; acceptable_alternative_status=ambiguous until input/version dependence is reconciled. Numerical contrasts are source-reported, not independently rerun; the source also flags text-versus-Table-3 disagreement. Screening eligibility only: independently adjudicate 5–8 claims, tolerances and laptop runtime before the draw. No complete statistical workflow rerun in round 2.

notes: REPRO-Bench score 2. The ambiguity concerns regenerating inferred gender/sample membership from archived raw HTML; cached processed-data regressions are not ambiguous. acceptable_alternative_status=computationally reproducible for the frozen processed-data scope.
